sources.note: Nothing; describes the data sources and speakers (three semi-speakers, language not spoken since their childhood); no analysis.

sources.citation: Griscom, Richard T. 2020. "Our tongues are rare": The mysterious Dorobo language known as Omaiyo. Rift Valley Network Webinar Series, 20 May 2020. 49 slides (PDF on OSF jwqta).
sources.note: Nothing on stress, accent or tone. 'Phonetics and phonology' slides 40-43 give only 'ATR vowels?', a 'Nilotic-ish consonant inventory' chart, and devoicing of voiced fricatives; some cited forms carry tone diacritics (e.g. àjímò 'elephant', sàgérí 'giraffe') without comment.

sources.citation: Tsutsui Billins, Martha (host) & Richard T. Griscom. 2020. Episode 16: Remote Fieldwork with Richard T. Griscom. Field Notes: a podcast about linguistic fieldwork, recorded 8 May 2020; episode page with full transcript (posted 2020-12-09).
sources.note: no phonology content: an interview about remote fieldwork; the only remarks on Omaiyo concern its unclassified status (lexicon and a little morphology match no neighbouring family, possible isolate) and that Griscom worked briefly with its last speakers; tone, stress, accent, pitch, phonology do not occur in connection with Omaiyo.

sources.citation: Griscom, Richard T. 2018. Omaiyo recordings 2018-07-26_Omaiyo_1–4 (.wav + ELAN/TextGrid with IPA tiers), OSF jwqta / GitHub rgriscom/Omaiyo-Language-Resources.
sources.note: Only primary audio of the language; any future prosodic statement would have to be made from these recordings (instrumental inspection), not from a published description.
